data.body_html:
Planning a yacht charter in Marbella for 2037? The good news: you don't need a boat license to enjoy the Mediterranean. At Boat Rental Marbella, every charter includes a licensed skipper, so you can skip the paperwork and focus on the views. Whether you're eyeing a 7m speedboat or a 29m superyacht, we cover the legal side. This guide explains the boat license requirements for Marbella yacht charter in 2037, what's changed, and how to get on the water today.

Do You Need a Boat License to Charter in Marbella?

No. If you charter through Boat Rental Marbella, you never need a license. All our boats come with a professional skipper who holds the necessary qualifications. This applies to every vessel in our fleet, from the compact Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) to the massive Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax). You just show up at Puerto Banús, and the skipper handles navigation, safety, and docking. It's the simplest way to explore the Costa del Sol without bureaucracy.

What Are the License Rules for Self-Driving in Spain?

If you plan to drive a boat yourself in Spanish waters, you need a valid recreational boating license. For boats up to 8m in length, a Patrón de Navegación Básica (Basic Navigation License) suffices. For vessels up to 12m, you need a Patrón de Embarcaciones de Recreo (PER). For boats over 12m, a Patrón de Yate is required. International licenses like the International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or RYA Day Skipper are also accepted for boats up to 24m, but you must carry the original document. However, most visitors prefer our skippered charters—no test, no fees, no hassle.

Boat License Requirements for Marbella 2037: What's Changed?

As of 2037, Spain's recreational boating regulations remain unchanged from 2025. The governing law is still Royal Decree 875/2014, which defines license categories and boat size limits. No major amendments have been introduced. This means the same rules apply: no license needed for skippered charters, and self-driving requires the appropriate permit. We stay updated on any changes, but for now, 2037 is business as usual. You can book with confidence.

What's Included in Every Charter?

Every booking comes with a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden fees. No surprise costs. You pay the quoted price and enjoy the day. For example, our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours—all inclusive. The Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for 4 hours and includes a free jet ski. For other boats, pricing is available on request via WhatsApp.

Why Charter Without a License in Marbella?

Marbella offers some of the best cruising grounds in Europe. From Puerto Banús to Cabopino, Estepona, and Sotogrande, the coastline is dotted with coves like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés. With a skipper, you can relax, swim, and sunbathe without worrying about navigation. The average summer temperature is 28°C, with calm seas. Plus, you avoid the cost and time of getting a Spanish license—perfect for short holidays.

How to Book Your License-Free Charter

Booking is straightforward. Visit our Marbella boat rental page, choose your boat, and select a date. We'll confirm your skipper and departure from Puerto Banús. Payment is secure, and cancellation is flexible. For questions about license requirements or boat availability, message us on WhatsApp. We're here to help you set sail in 2037.
